create.name: Chinmaya Mission Houston
create.bio:
Chinmaya Mission Houston is one of the longest-running Chinmaya centres in North America. It was set up in 1982 by Gaurang and Darshana Nanavaty, a married couple who left their careers to study Vedanta under Swami Chinmayananda and were later given the title of acharya by him. They still lead the centre, which now serves several hundred families from its own campus, Chinmaya Prabha, in Sugar Land on the south-western edge of Houston.

The heart of the week is Sunday. Adults gather for satsang in two morning sessions, with prayers, devotional singing and a talk from the acharyas on a scriptural text, while children from pre-school age to their late teens attend Bala Vihar, where stories, chanting, crafts and discussion introduce the values and culture of Indian tradition. Small study groups of five to fifteen people meet through the week to read and reflect on Vedantic texts together, and the centre runs a long series of Bhagavad Gita talks in Gujarati that is posted on its YouTube channel. The approach is non-dual Advaita Vedanta, presented as a practical philosophy open to people of any background and faith.

free_resources.title: Sunday Adult Satsanga
free_resources.description: Sunday discourses at the Chinmaya Smrti hall in Sugar Land, in two sessions (8:35 to 10:15 AM and 11:20 AM to 1:00 PM), with prayers, bhajans and a talk by the centre's acharyas.

free_resources.title: Study Groups
free_resources.description: Groups of between five and fifteen members who gather on a regular basis to read and talk through a Vedantic text together, each with a coordinator.

free_resources.title: Bala Vihar
free_resources.description: Weekly Sunday classes for children aged about five to seventeen, teaching Vedanta, values and Indian culture through stories, music, crafts and discussion.

Bala Vihar is listed free here but needs registration (non-refundable $25 per family with one or no child, max $50 for two or more children) and is waitlist-only for 2026-27.
